summary: The whole diff across both repos satisfies the task intent and all stated constraints. Backend: the immediate auto-link is replaced by a PENDING request + Approve/Reject flow on the reused single trainerLinks/{studentUid} doc (TRAINER_LINK_STATUSES adds 'pending'/'rejected', 'active' stays the approved state). requestTrainer soft-fails on invalid code (HTTP 200), is idempotent for same-trainer pending/active, returns already_linked (no silent switch) for an active link elsewhere, and writes status:'pending' with NO profile.trainerId mirror and NO totalStudents increment; approveRequest mirrors trainerId + trainerStatus:'approved' and increments the counter exactly once (guarded), rejectRequest only flips status. assertTrainerOwnsStudent is unchanged (still requires status==='active', so a pending link grants no data access) and a separate assertTrainerOwnsPendingRequest (404 anti-enumeration) gates approve/reject. The two entry points (POST /api/student/connect-trainer and /api/auth/link-trainer) now call requestTrainer. Backend field names referralCode/referralCodeLower/referralCodeUpdatedAt are stable; no new index needed; firebase/ was not committed. Backend lint+typecheck pass and 180 tests are green (trainerService 50, trainerRoutes 21). Frontend: a Requests tab with Approve/Reject wired to the real endpoints (invalidating both requests and students lists), a slimmed name+avatar Students card (tap still opens the real StudentDetailScreen), send-request UX in Profile/Register/Verify, a read-only My Trainer card that shows the connected Trainer Code only when active and 'Pending approval' while pending, and user-visible 'Referral Code'->'Trainer Code' renames with Dart identifiers/widget keys/backend fields left unchanged. SessionStore persists only firebaseUid/email/role as a startup hint (never token/password), is written fire-and-forget on verify-success and cleared on logout; the go_router redirect (lib/core/routing) is untouched so no new async gate exists, the local role never overrides the backend role, and there is no Firestore write on reopen. Both logout paths route through authController.logout, which clears the SessionStore and invalidates the full trainer provider tree (profile/students/requests/referral-code/tab/myTrainer + the per-student families) so no Trainer A data can leak to a later-logged-in User B. flutter analyze is clean and 129 flutter tests pass, including the new trainer_requests_test, my_trainer_model_test, and the logout-no-leak case in trainer_routing_test. No regressions observed in unrelated suites. No blocking findings remain.
